title: KYC Fraud — What Criminals Say and How to Stay Safe
text: KYC (Know Your Customer) fraud is one of the most common banking scams in India. Fraudsters send SMS or WhatsApp messages claiming your account will be 'blocked', 'suspended', or 'deactivated' unless you complete KYC immediately via a link or by sharing documents. These messages are fake. How to identify KYC fraud: (1) Urgency language — 'your account will be blocked in 24 hours', 'immediate action required', 'do it now or face penalty'. Legitimate KYC requests give weeks of notice through official bank channels. (2) Links to unofficial websites — your bank will never ask you to complete KYC via a bit.ly link or an unofficial domain. (3) Requests for OTP, PIN, or passwords during 'KYC'. These are never required for KYC. (4) Phone calls claiming to be from the bank asking you to 'complete KYC now'. Real bank staff do not make unsolicited calls for KYC. What to do: Ignore the message. If genuinely concerned, visit your bank branch with your original ID, or call the official number on the bank's official website. Never click links in KYC-related SMS. Report the number at cybercrime.gov.in.
